text: # Chicago Bulls

## Franchise History



The Chicago Bulls were founded on January 16, 1966. The team has won six
NBA championships, all during the 1990s: 1991, 1992, 1993, 1996, 1997, and
1998.

## First Three-Peat (1991-1993)



The core roster during the first three-peat was Michael Jordan, Scottie
Pippen, and Horace Grant, coached by Phil Jackson.

## Second Three-Peat (1996-1998)



The core roster during the second three-peat was Michael Jordan, Scottie
Pippen, and Dennis Rodman, coached by Phil Jackson. The 1995-96 team set an
NBA record with 72 regular-season wins, a record that stood until the
2015-16 season.

## Draft History



Notable draft picks in franchise history include Michael Jordan (1984, 3rd
overall), Scottie Pippen (1987, 5th overall, acquired via draft-night
trade), and Derrick Rose (2008, 1st overall).

## Retired Numbers



The Chicago Bulls have retired five jersey numbers: 1 (Derrick Rose), 4
(Jerry Sloan), 10 (Bob Love), 23 (Michael Jordan), and 33 (Scottie Pippen).

## Arenas



The Bulls played at the International Amphitheatre and Chicago Stadium
before moving to the United Center in 1994.
# Dennis Rodman

## Background



Dennis Rodman played college basketball at Southeastern Oklahoma State
University from 1983 to 1986, where he was a three-time NAIA All-American.
He was selected 27th overall in the 1986 NBA draft by the Detroit Pistons.

## NBA Career



Rodman played for the Detroit Pistons from 1986 to 1993, the San Antonio
Spurs from 1993 to 1995, the Chicago Bulls from 1995 to 1998, the Los
Angeles Lakers in 1999, and the Dallas Mavericks in 2000. His head coach in
Detroit was Chuck Daly; his head coach in San Antonio was Bob Hill; his
head coach in Chicago was Phil Jackson.

## Championships



Rodman won five NBA championships: 1989 and 1990 with the Detroit Pistons
under head coach Chuck Daly, and 1996, 1997, and 1998 with the Chicago
Bulls under head coach Phil Jackson.

## Awards



Rodman led the NBA in rebounding seven consecutive seasons, from 1992 to
1998. He won the NBA Defensive Player of the Year award in 1990 and 1991,
and was named to the All-Defensive First Team seven times.
# Michael Jordan

## Background



Michael Jordan attended the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
from 1981 to 1984. He was selected third overall in the 1984 NBA draft by
the Chicago Bulls.

## NBA Career



Jordan played for the Chicago Bulls from 1984 to 1993, and again from 1995
to 1998. He also played for the Washington Wizards from 2001 to 2003. His
head coaches with the Bulls were Doug Collins and later Phil Jackson.

## Championships



Jordan won six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls: 1991, 1992, and
1993 during the first three-peat, and 1996, 1997, and 1998 during the
second three-peat. He was named Finals MVP in all six of those series.

## Awards



Jordan won five NBA Most Valuable Player awards, the 1988 Defensive Player
of the Year award, and the 1985 Rookie of the Year award. He led the league
in scoring ten times.
# Phil Jackson

## Background



Phil Jackson attended the University of North Dakota from 1964 to 1967,
playing for the Fighting Sioux. He played in the NBA as a power forward for
the New York Knicks from 1967 to 1978 and the New Jersey Nets from 1978 to
1980, winning two championships as a player, in 1970 and 1973.

## Coaching Career



Jackson joined the Chicago Bulls as an assistant coach in 1987 and became
head coach in 1989, a role he held through 1998. He later coached the Los
Angeles Lakers from 1999 to 2004, and again from 2005 to 2011.

## Championships



As a head coach, Jackson won eleven NBA championships: six with the
Chicago Bulls (1991, 1992, 1993, 1996, 1997, 1998) and five with the Los
Angeles Lakers (2000, 2001, 2002, 2009, 2010). This is the most
championships won by a head coach in NBA history.

## Coaching Staff and Players



Tex Winter served as Jackson's lead assistant coach in Chicago and was the
architect of the triangle offense system Jackson's teams used. Jackson
coached Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen in Chicago, and later coached
Shaquille O'Neal, Kobe Bryant, and Pau Gasol in Los Angeles.
# Scottie Pippen

## Background



Scottie Pippen attended the University of Central Arkansas from 1983 to
1987. He was selected fifth overall in the 1987 NBA draft by the Seattle
SuperSonics, and was traded to the Chicago Bulls on draft night in exchange
for the eighth pick, Olden Polynice.

## NBA Career



Pippen played for the Chicago Bulls from 1987 to 1998, the Houston Rockets
in 1999, the Portland Trail Blazers from 1999 to 2003, and returned to the
Chicago Bulls from 2003 to 2004. His head coach for all six of his
championship seasons in Chicago was Phil Jackson.

## Championships



Pippen won six NBA championships, all with the Chicago Bulls: 1991, 1992,
1993, 1996, 1997, and 1998. He did not win a championship with Houston or
Portland.

## Awards



Pippen was a seven-time NBA All-Star and was named Most Valuable Player of
the 1994 All-Star Game. He was selected to the NBA All-Defensive First Team
eight times and won two Olympic gold medals, in 1992 and 1996. The Chicago
Bulls retired his jersey number, 33.
